choices.text: Shield it from the storm

effects.log: A blizzard comes. You stand over the lotus all night. In the morning it is whole. So are you, mostly.

variants: High on the glacier the snow lotus is open: it blooms once in thirty years and was blooming here before any sect came to this mountain. You have walked past it four times. This time you stop.
On the glacier the snow lotus has opened, as it does once in thirty years, as it did before any sect stood on this mountain. Four times you have hurried past it. Today you are not in a hurry.

events.text: The young head of a clan you destroyed two centuries ago comes to your mountain. {npc} is thirty, unarmed, and carries a tray of rice wine. {He} says {his} family has hated you for seven generations and {he} is tired of it.

choices.text: Accept the tray and make peace

effects.log: You pour for {him}, and drink tea yourself. You tell {npc} the truth of that night, the parts no one wrote down. {He} weeps, and then {he} laughs. The feud ends.

choices.text: Refuse. Some things should not be forgiven

effects.log: {npc} bows and leaves the tray. You sit with it for a long time. You do not drink it, and you do not pour it out.

choices.text: Apologise first, before {he} speaks

effects.log: {npc} drops the tray. Two hundred years of hate meet one sentence and simply stop. You both sit down on the step, stunned.

events.text: The sect you founded is older now than the kingdom it stands in. Its elders run it like a court. Every new disciple receives a tablet with your face on it. You walk through the gate in plain clothes and the gatekeeper asks you for an entry fee.
events.arc: Founder of a Sect Older Than a Kingdom

choices.text: Pay the fee and look around

effects.log: Two coppers. Inside, things are good and bad as things always are. You leave a list of twenty corrections on the head elder's desk.

choices.text: Show the gatekeeper the founder's seal

effects.log: The gatekeeper faints. The bells ring. A thousand disciples kneel in rows. You wish you had paid the fee.

choices.text: Hire on as a gardener for a year

effects.log: Nobody knows. You hear everything. The young disciples are kind to the old gardener. That tells you more than any report.

events.text: There is a festival now on your birthday. Nobody knows your real birthday, so they guessed. They guessed wrong. There are dumplings in a shape that is meant to be your sword, and a dance about your famous duel that ends with everyone falling over.

choices.text: Go, and dance the dance

effects.log: You fall over at exactly the right time. The village loves you. Nobody guesses. Next year you are invited by name as the old one who dances well.

choices.text: Tell them your real birthday

effects.log: They thank you politely and keep their date. It has been the festival for eighty years. Your birthday is the wrong one now.

choices.text: Send a gift of rice for the festival

effects.log: Ten taels of rice, anonymously. The festival is twice as big. Rumour says the master sent it. Rumour, for once, is right.

variants: The town keeps a festival on your birthday, which nobody knows, so they chose a day, and it is the wrong one. There are dumplings shaped like your sword and a dance about your great duel in which everyone falls down.

events.text: A strange heaviness has settled on you. Not illness. Not grief. A grey weight, like an old coat. Masters your age, the ones who stopped moving, sit in caves and turn to stone. You see the first grey dust on your sleeve.

choices.text: Take a new apprentice tomorrow

effects.log: A loud, clumsy, curious child. Within a month the grey weight is gone. You are too busy shouting about posture to turn to stone.

choices.text: Walk to the sea, a thousand li

effects.log: Every day a new road. At the sea you stand in the waves until your feet are numb. The weight washes off somewhere along the way.

choices.text: Sit in the dust and examine it

effects.log: It is only stillness, gone stale. You breathe into it until it moves. Then you get up and sweep the floor. Movement is the cure.

variants: A grey weight has come over you, not sickness and not sorrow, more like an old coat you cannot take off. The masters of your age who stopped moving sit in caves and turn to stone. This morning there is grey dust on your sleeve.

Something grey has settled on you, heavier than tiredness and quieter than grief. In the caves of the mountain the masters of your age who stopped moving have become stone. There is grey dust on your sleeve this morning.

events.text: Three masters of the Bone Lantern sect surround you in the marsh at dusk. They have heard that the qi of a master past three centuries is the greatest elixir. They are wrong. They will not listen. Mist rises between the reeds.

choices.text: Fight them in the mist

ok.log: Three shapes in the mist, then two, then none. You walk out of the marsh at dawn, mud to the knee, all of you where you belong.

fail.log: They are good, and there are three. You get out of the marsh, but they leave marks. (-30 health)

choices.text: Explain, patiently, that it does not work

effects.log: Surprisingly, the youngest believes you. The other two argue with each other. You walk away while they argue.

choices.text: Vanish into the reeds

effects.log: You lie face down in cold water for four hours. They search until midnight. You go home, wet and annoyed, and alive.

variants: Mist on the marsh at dusk, and three masters of the Bone Lantern sect step out of it around you. They believe the qi of a master past three centuries is the greatest elixir. They are wrong, and they will not listen.
The reeds part and three Bone Lantern masters close in. Someone told them the qi of a master as old as you would make them immortal. It would not. They have not come to hear that.
Dusk on the marsh, and three Bone Lantern masters close in through the reeds, sure that the qi of one as old as you is the elixir of long life. It is not. They have not come to be told so.

events.text: A shrine to you has a keeper now. {npc}, a solemn young person who sweeps it, polishes your stone face and scolds pilgrims who touch the nose for luck. {He} has no idea that the old visitor who comes on rainy days is the face {he} polishes.

choices.text: Keep visiting as a stranger

effects.log: Every rainy day. {npc} brings you tea now, because you are old and wet. You talk about everything except the statue.

choices.text: Touch the nose for luck

effects.log: {npc} scolds you thoroughly. You apologise. You come back next week and do it again. It becomes your joke, though {he} does not know it.

choices.text: Leave money for the roof

effects.log: The roof is repaired by summer. {npc} never learns who paid. {He} thanks the statue every morning. Close enough.

events.text: A warlord's soldiers want to tear down the shrine for stone to build a fort. {npc}, grey at the temples now, stands in front of it with a broom. Twelve soldiers. One broom. You are watching from the road.

choices.text: Stand beside {npc}

effects.log: You stand with {npc}. The soldiers look at you, at the statue, at you. Their captain goes pale and orders them back. {npc} turns to you, very slowly.

choices.text: Let {npc} handle it, and help a little

effects.log: Every soldier who lifts a hammer finds it suddenly too heavy. They leave, unnerved. {npc} thinks the statue did it. In a way.

choices.text: Tell {npc} who you are, right now

effects.log: {npc} looks at you, then the statue, then you. Then {he} turns back to the soldiers with a very different face. They run.

events.text: {npc} is very old now and cannot sweep. {He} sits on the shrine step in the sun while a grandchild does it, badly. {He} asks you to sit down. "I always knew," {npc} says. "From the first rainy day. You touch your nose when you lie."

choices.text: Laugh, and touch your nose

effects.npcPass: old age, on the shrine step in the sun
effects.log: You both laugh until {npc} has to stop for breath. {He} dies that winter, peacefully. You carve a small statue of {him} beside yours.

choices.text: Thank {him} for the years

effects.log: "It was a good job," {npc} says. "Quiet. Good company." {He} dies before spring. The grandchild keeps the shrine now.

choices.text: Teach the grandchild the broom stroke

effects.npcPass: old age, watching a grandchild sweep
effects.log: From the hip. {npc} watches, nodding, eyes half closed in the sun. {He} is gone by the next rainy day.

events.text: You are the oldest of the Ten Greatest now. The second oldest died this spring. At the council, the eight others look at you differently. As if you are the last pillar of an old house. As if they are waiting to see whether you will fall.

choices.text: Take charge of the council

effects.log: You speak first and last. Nobody objects. You did not want this. Now you have it. The murim notices at once.

choices.text: Stay quiet and watch the others

effects.log: Two of them are already planning for the day after you. One is plotting. One is kind. You note which is which.

choices.text: Announce you will step down soon

effects.log: Panic. Then relief. Then intrigue. You did not mean it. You enjoy watching them.

variants: The second oldest of the Ten Greatest died this spring, and now you are the oldest. At the council the others watch you as people watch the last beam of an old hall, waiting to see if it holds.

events.text: One of the Ten is plotting. A master of two hundred, hungry for your place. Poison in the council tea, the rumour says, and a young killer hired in the capital. Your chair is very old and very comfortable.

choices.text: Drink the tea anyway

ok.log: You drink it slowly while looking the plotter in the eye. You burn the poison out. The plotter resigns that afternoon.

fail.deathCause: poisoned tea at the council of the Ten Greatest
fail.log: The poison is better than the rumour said. You burn most of it out. Most. (-32 health)

choices.text: Expose the plot in open council

effects.log: Evidence, witnesses, the killer's letter. The plotter is cast out of the Ten. You feel no triumph. Only tired.

choices.text: Visit the plotter, alone, at night

effects.log: A long talk. The plotter is afraid of dying unremembered. You understand that. You help them write their book. The plot ends.

events.text: The Ten gather for a portrait. You stand in the centre. Around you, nine masters, all younger, all of them taught by somebody you taught. The painter asks you to look wise. You decide what this council will be after you are gone.

choices.text: Write the council's new charter

effects.log: Twelve rules. The first says: the oldest does not rule. The council will last longer than you. That is the point.

choices.text: Name a successor in front of all

effects.log: The kind one. The others nod. You feel the old house shift its weight onto a new pillar. It holds.

choices.text: Just smile for the painter

effects.log: The portrait is famous for centuries: nine stern masters and one old one, grinning. Nobody knows what you were thinking.

variants: A painter sets up for the Ten's portrait, with you in the middle and nine masters round you, every one of them taught by someone you taught. "Look wise," says the painter. You think about what this council will be when you are gone.

events.text: Black clouds gather over your mountain. Not weather. The heavens have noticed how long you have lived and are considering whether to object. The village below has already started packing.

choices.text: Stand on the peak and meet it

ok.log: Nine strikes. You take them all. Your hair stands up for a week. The heavens grumble off. The village unpacks.

fail.deathCause: lightning from a heaven that thought you had lived long enough
fail.log: The ninth strike finds you wanting. (-35 health)

choices.text: Shield the village first

effects.log: You spread your qi over the village like a roof. The lightning hits the mountain, not the houses. You are tired for a year.

choices.text: Sit in a cave and wait it out

effects.log: The heavens are patient. You are more patient. After a week of thunder the clouds give up. You go back to bed.

variants: Black clouds pile up over your mountain, and it is not weather. Heaven has noticed how long you have lived and is deciding whether to object. The village below is already loading its carts.
The sky over your peak goes black at noon. Heaven has been counting your years and does not like the total. Down in the village, the carts are already being packed.
Black cloud gathers over your mountain with no wind to bring it. Heaven has noticed your age and is deciding what it thinks of it. In the village below, the carts are already loaded.

events.text: Someone built you a tomb, long ago, when they thought you had died. Grave robbers are digging into it tonight. You are standing behind them, watching. They are arguing about whether your bones will be worth more than your sword.

choices.text: Tap one on the shoulder

effects.log: The robber turns, sees the face from the tomb mural, and faints. The other two run so fast they leave their shoes.

choices.text: Let them in. Watch them find it empty

effects.log: No bones, no sword, only a sign you put in long ago: try again later. They stare at it, then at each other, then flee.

choices.text: Hire them to fill it in

effects.log: Five taels for honest work. They are confused and grateful. One of them now sweeps your tomb on feast days.

variants: Long ago someone built you a tomb, believing you dead. Tonight robbers are digging into it, and you are standing just behind them in the dark, listening to them argue whether your bones or your sword will fetch more.

events.text: An old tea master in the valley has been perfecting one blend for sixty years. {npc} brings you the first cup. {He} says only someone who has lived a very long life can tell {him} if it is finished.

choices.text: Drink it slowly and tell the truth

effects.log: It is almost perfect. Almost. You tell {npc} which hill the last leaf should come from. {He} bows to the ground.

choices.text: Say it is perfect

effects.log: {npc} cries with joy and gives you a whole tin. It is not perfect. But {he} is sixty years tired, and the tea is very good.

choices.text: Brew {him} a cup of yours

effects.log: Your tea is simple. {npc} drinks it and is silent a long time. "I added too much," {he} says at last. {He} starts again, happily.

events.text: A child of thirteen has walked for a year to find the legendary master on the mountain. {npc} has walked through three provinces, two wars and one very bad winter. {His} sandals are gone. {He} asks you if the master is home.
events.arc: A Pilgrim Who Walked a Year

choices.text: Admit it is you

effects.log: {npc} does not believe you. You are too ordinary. You make {him} soup. After the soup {he} believes you a little more.

choices.text: Say the master is away, and take {him} in

effects.log: {npc} waits for the master for a year, learning from the kind old caretaker. At the end, you tell {him}. {He} is furious for an hour.

choices.text: Give {him} sandals and a letter home

effects.log: "The walk was the lesson." {npc} does not understand. {He} will, at about forty. You put an extra rice ball in {his} pack.

events.text: On a far peak you find another ancient master. {npc} has been sitting in the same spot for forty years. Moss on {his} shoulders, a bird's nest in {his} hair. {He} opens one eye and says, "Oh. You. Still walking about?"

choices.text: Sit beside {him} for a season

effects.log: Neither of you speaks for three months. It is the best conversation you have had in years. The birds raise two broods.

choices.text: Persuade {him} to come down

effects.log: {npc} grumbles, sheds the moss, and walks down with you. In the valley {he} eats nine dumplings and cries. {He} had forgotten dumplings.

choices.text: Spar, just one exchange

ok.log: One exchange. The peak loses a boulder. {npc} closes {his} eye again, satisfied. "Still walking, then. Good."

fail.log: {npc} was not asleep. Not at all. You fly off the peak and land in a pine. (-15 health)

events.text: A new sect in the east teaches a technique called the Broken Crane. It is your old crane form, done wrong, exactly the way you did it wrong at thirty before you fixed it. Someone copied you on a bad day. It has two thousand disciples.
events.arc: A Sect Founded on Your Mistake

choices.text: Visit and correct it

effects.log: The founder is horrified, then fascinated. The Broken Crane becomes the Mended Crane. The disciples complain about relearning everything.

choices.text: Study the wrong version for its own sake

effects.log: They have built forty years of art on your mistake. Some of it works. A mistake, it turns out, is also a road.

choices.text: Laugh and leave them to it

effects.log: Two thousand people doing your bad day perfectly. It is the funniest thing you have seen in years. You laugh all the way home.

events.text: You catch your reflection in a still pond. You have not looked properly in decades. The face is the face of a forty-year-old. The eyes are not. The eyes look like the pond: deep, cold, full of things that sank long ago.

choices.text: Look until you know the face

effects.log: A long hour. The eyes soften as you watch. Maybe they only needed someone to look at them.

choices.text: Smile at it until it smiles back

effects.log: It takes a while. The face in the pond is out of practice. In the end it smiles, a little crooked. Better.

choices.text: Throw a stone in

effects.log: Ripples. Gone. You walk on. Some things are better not stared at too long.

events.text: A bowl of noodles costs eight coppers. When you were young it cost one. You stand at the stall and argue with the noodle seller for a full minute before you realise you are arguing with a price that died eighty years ago.

choices.text: Pay, and tip generously

effects.log: The noodle seller had braced for a fight. Instead you overpay and apologise. You become a favourite customer.

choices.text: Teach the seller the old broth recipe

effects.log: Bones, simmered all night, a little dried fish. The seller tries it and doubles the price. Fair.

choices.text: Go home and cook for yourself

effects.log: Your noodles cost nothing and taste of long ago. You eat them alone, very content, and a little smug.

events.text: Your fishing rod is a hundred years old. You have replaced the line forty times, the hook two hundred times and the handle twice. A fisherman at the lake says it is not the same rod at all. You disagree. You think about it all afternoon.

choices.text: Decide the rod is the fishing

effects.log: Not wood, not line. The rod is the habit of sitting here. In that sense you have only ever had one. The fisherman thinks you are mad.

choices.text: Catch a fish to settle it

effects.log: A fat carp. The fisherman concedes, rod or no rod, that you know where the fish are. You cook it together.

choices.text: Give the rod to the fisherman

effects.log: "Now it is a new rod." The fisherman laughs. You walk home with your hands empty and a strange lightness.

events.text: The inn on the high pass where you stayed at twenty is still there. Fifth innkeeper since then. The same smoky beams. The same draughty corner bed. A carving you made on the bedpost is still there: a rude drawing of a teacher you disliked.

choices.text: Sand the carving off

effects.log: A hundred years of guests have seen your bad drawing. You sand it off, a bit ashamed, a bit nostalgic. The teacher would have laughed.

choices.text: Add a kinder drawing beside it

effects.log: The same teacher, smiling this time. The innkeeper says guests now argue about which is the true face. Both, you think.

choices.text: Tell the innkeeper the story

effects.log: The innkeeper laughs until tears come and charges you nothing for the room. The bedpost becomes the inn's most famous feature.

events.text: A tiger crosses your path in the mountains, old and lame, its ribs showing. It has been raiding the village goats. The hunters want it dead. It looks at you the way you sometimes look at mirrors: tired of being strong.

choices.text: Drive it away gently

effects.log: A push of qi, like a hand on the shoulder. The tiger goes deeper into the mountains. The goats are safe. The tiger, for a while longer, is too.

choices.text: End it quickly, mercifully

effects.log: One blow, no pain. The hunters thank you. You sit with the tiger a while. You both had good long runs.

choices.text: Feed it, once

effects.log: A goat you buy from the village. The tiger eats and looks at you for a long time. Then it is gone. The raids stop. Nobody knows why.

events.text: You realise one evening that you are the last person alive who knows the Flowing Cloud Palm. It was common once. Every village had a teacher. Now there is nobody but you. If you forget it, or die, it is gone.
events.arc: A Forgotten Art Only You Know

choices.text: Teach it to anyone who will learn

effects.log: A blacksmith, two farmers and a curious old widow. Not elegant. But the art lives in four more bodies now. Enough.

choices.text: Write it down in full

effects.log: Three months, thirty pages, every breath noted. Paper is not a body. But paper keeps.

choices.text: Let it go when you go

effects.log: Arts are born and die like people. Something else will grow in its place. You practise it once more, alone, very slowly.

events.text: The harbour town you knew is two li inland now. The sea moved away. Fishing boats rot in fields of wheat. The old people still walk to the edge of town at dawn to look at where the water used to be.

choices.text: Walk with them to the old shore

effects.log: You stand in a wheat field at dawn with twenty old people, looking at nothing. It is one of the most peaceful mornings of your life.

choices.text: Follow the sea to where it went

effects.log: Two li. The new shore is young, raw sand and loud gulls. Even the sea changes address. You wade in up to your knees and laugh.

choices.text: Help build the new harbour

effects.log: Stone by stone, a season of work. The town moves to the water. The old boats stay in the wheat, like monuments.

variants: The harbour town you knew now stands two li from the sea. The water simply left. Boats lie rotting in the wheat, and at dawn the old people still walk to the edge of town to look at where the sea used to be.

The sea has walked two li away from the harbour town you knew. Boats sit in the wheat with their ribs showing, and every dawn the old people go to the end of the street to look at where the water was.
